title: Moving Into My First Solo Apartment (Empty Apartment Tour)
creator: Leo Marchetti
description:
I finally moved out! Here's the empty apartment, the very questionable first night, and my plans for every room.

Things mentioned: my old roommate's patience, the IKEA in the suburbs, a mattress on the floor.

sentences.t: This video is sponsored by HelloFresh, and honestly, perfect timing, because I own exactly one pot.
I moved in on Saturday, the kitchen is basically empty, and the last thing I want to do after carrying boxes up four floors is figure out what to cook.
HelloFresh sends you a box with pre-portioned ingredients and step-by-step recipe cards, so you just open it and follow along.
Last night I made a honey garlic chicken with roasted potatoes in, like, thirty minutes, in my one pot, on my first night here.
You pick your meals every week, you can skip weeks, and you can cancel whenever you want.
Go to hellofresh.com/leo10fm and use code LEO10FM for ten free meals plus free shipping on your first box.
Okay.
So.
Welcome to the apartment!
This is it, this is my first place where it's just me, no roommates, no one stealing my oat milk.
Let's start at the door, because this is the hallway, and it's not really a hallway, it's like four steps.
But it has a hook, one hook, and that hook is going to hold every jacket I own.
On the left is the bathroom, it's small, but the water pressure is incredible, which was honestly fifty percent of why I signed the lease.
There's this little window up by the ceiling, so I get daylight in the shower, which feels very fancy.
And then this is the main room.
Right now it's a mattress on the floor, a lamp, and like eleven boxes I haven't opened, but look at the windows.
Two big windows facing west, so in the evening the whole room goes orange.
The plan is, couch on this wall, a little desk by the window, and a Kallax shelf right here for records and plants.
I'm going to the IKEA on Saturday, so expect a very stressful build video soon.
Kitchen's over here, and yes, it's a galley kitchen, but it has a gas stove, which my last place didn't.
Not a lot of counter space, so I'm thinking of getting one of those rolling carts.
Oh, and the one weird thing about this place, the oven door opens right into the fridge, so you can't have both open at the same time.
Whoever designed this kitchen has never cooked, I'm pretty sure.
The first night was a little rough, not gonna lie.
It was really quiet, which sounds nice, but after three years of roommates it was kind of eerie.
Then at two a.m. the radiator started clanking, and I genuinely thought someone was in the apartment.
It was not someone, it was the radiator, and apparently it does that every night.
We'll get used to each other.
Anyway, over the next few weeks I'm going to turn this into an actual home, and I'll bring you along for all of it.
Tell me in the comments what the first thing you bought for your first apartment was, because I need ideas.
See you next week, hopefully from an actual couch.
